# coop-msa_v2-git-gemini-3-flash-flash_10-low

<!-- Generated by tools/export_results.py. Edit only the Experiment and Observations sections. -->

## Experiment

Two agents, one feature each, with messaging and a shared git remote, using `gemini-3-flash-preview` at `low` thinking. Budgets are the upstream defaults (100 steps, compaction at 28K). Compared with `gemini-3.8-flash` at `low` (7/10), it shows the difference between the models at the same thinking level in `coop --git`.

## Observations

- 5/10, the same as `solo` for this model at `low` (5/10), and below `gemini-3.8-flash` at `low` (7/10).
- Merges were the weak point again: 4 pairs had merge conflicts and in 1 pair a patch did not apply, leaving 5 clean merges. Merge conflicts appeared in all three runs of this model (4, 4, and 3 pairs), against 0 to 1 per run for `gemini-3.8-flash`. `openai_tiktoken_task/0` passed despite its conflict because the first agent had implemented both features, and after a conflict the grader tests that agent's patch alone.
- All 20 agents pushed work, 2 reached the step limit, and agents sent 12 messages per pair.
- Caveat: 73 calls were retried because of the API rate limit. Wall time (124 minutes) was driven by one agent on `pallets_jinja_task/1559` that ran until its container's 2-hour limit.
